flashcard_questions.q: Which 1929 event destroyed the optimism of the 1920s worldwide?
How many Germans were unemployed by 1932?
Which region of north-eastern China did Japan invade in 1931?
Why did the Japanese military argue for seizing Manchuria?
flashcard_questions.a: Territorial expansion would give Japan resource-rich land.

flashcard_questions.q: What was the Mukden Incident of September 1931?
flashcard_questions.a: A staged explosion on the South Manchuria Railway, blamed on Chinese saboteurs.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Chinese city did Japan bomb in February 1932?
What name did Japan give to its puppet state in Manchuria?
Who was placed on the throne of Manchukuo as a figurehead?
flashcard_questions.a: Pu Yi, the former Chinese emperor.

flashcard_questions.q: Which commission did the League send to investigate Japan’s invasion?
What did the Lytton Report of October 1932 conclude?
What was the League’s vote on the Lytton Report?
In ____, Japan walked out of the League and invaded Jehol.
How did the League punish Japan for invading Manchuria?
flashcard_questions.a: It imposed no sanctions and took no military action.

flashcard_questions.q: Why would economic sanctions against Japan have been meaningless?
flashcard_questions.a: Japan’s main trading partner, the USA, was not in the League.

notes: 14 cards: 5 event/date (1 cloze on March 1933), 3 figure, 3 term/name, 3 cause-effect. Left the 'protectionism' glossary term out as it is covered by the sanctions card.
